solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: So, do for corpse's false teeth?

definitions.note: teeth are what we process food with, hence the question mark; the answer is plural to match

indicators.note: false teeth are not the real thing, so the letters of the preceding words are made up into something new

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dead body's dentures could do the job of the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false teeth' reads as one phrase, but 'false' is the anagram signal working on SO DO FOR CORPSES, and 'teeth?' alone is the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth chew and grind what we eat, so they are jokingly kitchen machines that chop and blend meals.

clue.text: Old boy with valet, or similar, taking notice

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a valet is one kind of servant

explanation.surface: A former pupil and his manservant pay close attention to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant is alert and watchful, quick to notice details around them.

clue.text: Stayed in deserted European's world

parts.note: D is a recognised abbreviation for deserted, as in old military records
Welt is the German word for world, so a European (a German) would say it

explanation.surface: Someone remained in the world of a European who had been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: WELT is German for world; a German is the 'European' here.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or reside somewhere, so the past tense means remained or resided.

clue.text: Gets in honest practice

indicators.note: in tells us the first word's letters sit within the word for honest

parts.note: real means genuine, honest
to get someone is to hear them, as in 'I hear you'

explanation.surface: Someone takes part in a genuine training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' means understands, as in 'I hear what you are saying'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a run-through or trial performance done before the real show.

clue.text: Weep over personal trainer's vault

indicators.note: in a down clue the first word sits over, above, what follows it

parts.note: to weep is to cry
PT is short for personal trainer (or physical training)

explanation.surface: Someone sobs over their fitness coach's gymnastic vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' looks like the gym leap a trainer would teach, but it is the underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground chamber beneath a church, a burial vault.

clue.text: Mostly agreed terms for cribs in the theatre

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sure! means agreed, yes
titles are terms, the names by which things are called

explanation.surface: A contract whose terms were largely settled, perhaps for babies' beds.
explanation.walkthrough: A crib is a translation or aid used to cheat; in opera houses the translation is projected above the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Surtitles are translated captions projected above a stage so the audience can follow a foreign-language opera.

clue.text: Rejecting odd spots woman spies a haven of calm?

indicators.note: throwing out the letters in odd positions leaves the even ones, the 2nd, 4th and so on

explanation.surface: A woman turns down blemished places and finds a peaceful retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a fertile spot in a desert, and figuratively any peaceful refuge from turmoil.

clue.text: Fiercely foxy about hype

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for foxy goes round the other

parts.note: foxy means cunning, sly
to tout is to promote noisily, to hype

explanation.surface: A cunning person reacts ferociously to all the publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoutly means resolutely or vigorously, as in a stoutly defended position.

clue.text: Community leaders being lousy golfers taking time off

indicators.note: taking ... off together signal that a letter is removed
off completes the instruction to take a letter away

parts.note: in golf and other games a rabbit is a poor player

explanation.surface: Local leaders who are hopeless at golf take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: A rabbit is sporting slang, chiefly British, for a poor player.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is the religious leader and teacher of a Jewish congregation.

clue.text: Is cracking booze the way for intended union members?

definitions.text: the way for intended union members?

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: ale is beer, booze

explanation.surface: Getting into the drink is how engaged couples make their way to the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'union' is a marriage and its intended members are bride and groom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride walks down the central passage of a church to her wedding, the route for a couple about to marry.

clue.text: Illusionist's revealing shriek he's dressed with poetry

indicators.note: dressed means prepared or arranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A magician cries out at the reveal, his patter decked out in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the exclamation a conjuror makes as a trick is completed, like 'abracadabra'.

clue.text: Cap for service leader? Black one given to retired volunteers?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral one
TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A hat for whoever leads a ceremony, handed out to former volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'service' is a church service, not the armed forces the volunteers suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square stiff cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy who lead worship.

clue.text: Triumph in trial turned over gear that comes as a pair

definitions.text: gear that comes as a pair

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the turned trial word
turned over means flipped, so the word for trial reads backwards

parts.note: a test is a trial
a win is a triumph

explanation.surface: A victory after a trial overturned on appeal, with matching kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching jumper and cardigan sold and worn together, clothing in two pieces.

clue.text: Keen son gets mouth organ

parts.note: harp is slang for a harmonica, especially among blues players

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic boy is given a harmonica.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and sharp both describe a fine cutting edge or a quick mind.

clue.text: Fleece is for, well, always

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
fit means well, healthy
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A woolly jacket is good for staying healthy all the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like the garment but is the verb to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To profiteer is to make excessive gains by overcharging, which is to fleece customers.

clue.text: Reliable child, I look after chargers and such like

definitions.text: I look after chargers and such like

parts.note: stable means steady, reliable
a boy is a male child

explanation.surface: A dependable youngster says they care for phone chargers and similar gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chargers' suggests phone leads; here they are horses, as a charger is a warhorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable lad tends horses, and a charger is a cavalry horse, so the first-person definition describes the job.

clue.text: Meet anger anew in consensus

indicators.note: anew means made again in a fresh form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People meet a fresh wave of fury while trying to reach a common view.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement and consensus both mean a shared opinion held by everyone involved.

clue.text: With dance I earn fantastically

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: done fantastically means in a wild, fanciful way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer boasts of making a fortune from dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: With BALL first, the anagram of I EARN gives ERINA; the whole clue is also what such a dancer might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a professional female ballet dancer, who earns her living through dance.

clue.text: Kitty, tough old bird, producer of pulp fiction, say

parts.note: a pot is a kitty, a pool of money
a boiler is an old hen fit only for boiling

explanation.surface: A cat and a battle-axe of a woman as hack writers.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiler is a tough old hen that must be stewed, and also British slang for an unattractive older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a work, or a writer, turned out quickly just to earn money, like cheap sensational fiction.

clue.text: Butcher sells this dressing for crown

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pastry case filled with chopped pork, sold by British butchers
second meaning: a hat with a flat top and turned-up brim, worn on the head (crown)

explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests a sauce for meat, but it is something you dress the crown of your head with.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a raised British meat pie and a low flat-crowned hat.

clue.text: Fifty inside plane? It's do with the sun

indicators.note: inside means within, so the numeral goes into the other word

parts.note: to plane is to glide or soar
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people on an aircraft wonder whether it runs on sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the verb to glide, not the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar is an adjective meaning relating to or derived from our star.

clue.text: Shop that girl more readily

parts.note: to shop someone is British slang for informing on them, to rat
her refers to that girl

explanation.surface: Someone would prefer to betray that girl to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: To shop someone, in British slang, is to inform on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather means preferably, as in 'I would rather go', so sooner or more willingly.

clue.text: What needs doing at this university?

definitions.text: What needs doing at this university?

parts.words: What needs doing at this university?
parts.note: the study every student must do at college is also the name of a university town in Berkshire

explanation.walkthrough: Students 'read' their subject at British universities, and there is a University of Reading in the town of that name west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the activity of studying books and the name of an English university town.

clue.text: Tart is caught in flat

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the word for flat

parts.note: arid means dull, flat
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pastry sits trapped in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like the pastry but is the adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid and tart both describe a sharp, bitter, unpleasant taste or smell.

clue.text: Visitor thought out loud

indicators.note: out loud means spoken, so we want a word sounding like the one for thought

parts.note: guessed means supposed, thought

explanation.surface: A caller voices their thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone invited to stay or dine at another person's home.

clue.text: Famous hospital dept absorbing damaging charge

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the department's letters surround the charge

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a mine is an explosive charge that does damage

explanation.surface: A well-known hospital unit faces a harmful accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an accusation or fee, but it is an explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means distinguished and well known, prominent in a field.

clue.text: Early Americans during lawsuit stopped before finishing

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: halted before the end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Native peoples whose legal action was halted midway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people ruled a great Andean empire in South America before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: A stern and mean business

parts.note: per means a, each, as in 'ten pounds a head'
severe means stern

explanation.surface: A strict boss is serious about getting things done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean business' reads as a stingy firm but is the idiom for being determined.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, showing you are determined.

clue.text: What's central to Detective Frost?

indicators.note: central means at the middle, so we take the middle letter of the nine-letter word

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: What lies at the heart of the TV police drama about Inspector Frost?
explanation.walkthrough: A Touch of Frost was a British TV detective series; every episode turns on an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Detective stories revolve around an offence to be solved, so it is central to any sleuth's work.

clue.text: Father of the House perhaps lets trade names slip

indicators.note: slip means go wrong or slide out of place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior politician lets the names of trades slip out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Father of the House is the longest-serving MP in the UK House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran respected politician is an example of this, as the longest-serving MP is.
